name: Derivatives-implied relative value (options, futures, merger-arb spreads vs Polymarket)
one_line: Price 'above/hits X by date' and earnings markets off listed option surfaces, sell the persistently rich YES, optionally hedge with verticals or perps.
scope: Cover the replication toolkit (vertical/width for terminal, ~2x delta or reflection for one-touch, SVI/SSVI plus Breeden-Litzenberger), measured wedges (BTC +5.6-6.3 pp vs Binance options, +11 pp vs Deribit, half-life ~4 h, 2023 sample; gold +8.9 pp, silver +5.3 pp, 2026), the reality check that much of it is variance-risk plus longshot premium, worked practitioner trades (IBIT call spread vs '$110k by March'), earnings hybrids (TSLA beat rate vs market odds), basis risks (Chainlink/Binance reference vs option index, expiry mismatch), 100% collateral with no cross-margin, fee 0.04-0.07, and Polymarket Perps as a same-collateral delta hedge. Boundary: pure ladder monotonicity checks are combinatorial-logical-arbitrage; unhedged longshot selling is longshot-selling-flb; perps venue economics are perps-lp-rewards-basis.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Options-implied pricing of finance / crypto-threshold / earnings markets
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Price 'above X by date' and earnings-move markets off listed options (Deribit/Binance/CME/equity options) and trade the gap, hedging in options or Polymarket Perps.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Convert the options surface into risk-neutral probabilities for the Polymarket strike/date and compare with the book; a paper finds a mean gap of 5.6-6.3 percentage points between Binance-options-implied and Polymarket BTC threshold prices. For earnings, combine historical beat rates and implied moves (TSLA: beats 38% historically vs 73% market price) and optionally pair a Polymarket leg with straddles/calls. Polymarket's own perps venue (launched 2026-09-03, up to 20x on BTC/ETH, ~10x equities) now offers an in-account delta hedge in the same collateral.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: A deep external derivatives market pricing the same distribution.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: Retail prices these by narrative; but finance is the most efficient category (maker-taker gap only 0.17pp on Kalshi), so expect thin, competitive edges.
raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Risk-neutral vs real-world probability wedge, settlement-source differences (Chainlink TWAP vs exchange index), fees 0.04 + hedge costs, small depth, the cited gap sample is old (2023 contracts).
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Daily snapshot of Deribit-implied probabilities vs Polymarket crypto threshold markets for 30 days; measure convergence PnL of fading gaps >4pp net of fees.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Options-implied vs prediction-market probability convergence (BTC, gold, silver thresholds)
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Polymarket 'above X by date' contracts trade 5-9 points rich to option-implied risk-neutral probabilities; sell the rich YES and delta-hedge or pair with a digital replicated from listed options.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Compute the risk-neutral probability of each threshold from the option surface (Binance/Deribit for BTC, CME for gold/silver), compare with the Polymarket mid, and sell YES (buy NO) when the gap exceeds costs; hedge delta with futures or a tight call spread. The gap mean-reverts with an AR(1) half-life of ~4 hours for BTC and <3 days for metals, and is largest when the option-implied probability is low and expiry is far (longshot-style demand).
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Retail speculative demand for out-of-the-money upside on Polymarket versus professionally arbitraged option surfaces.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: Requires options infrastructure and cross-margin that most Polymarket participants lack; the hedge turns a directional longshot-selling trade into relative value.

evidence.title: Do Prediction Markets Match Option Prices? Bitcoin Threshold Evidence from Binance and Polymarket (Portnaya), arXiv
evidence.supports: Mean gap +5.58 pp (main contract, 214 hourly obs) and +6.33 pp pooled (287 obs); +11.05 pp vs Deribit; AR(1) 0.849, half-life ~4.2 h; delta-hedged backtest 16 trades, net alpha 0.067, t=2.10, p=0.053, win rate 69%, median hold 3.5 h. Data are Aug-Sep 2023 [pre-2025 sample, possibly stale] and n is small.

evidence.title: Prediction Markets vs. Options-Implied Probabilities: Evidence from Gold and Silver Futures (Carpenter), Zenodo
evidence.supports: 2,671 daily observations on 24 CME-threshold contracts over six months: Polymarket overprices upside by 8.9 pp (gold) and 5.3 pp (silver); AR(1) half-lives under three days; divergence shrinks toward expiry; presented as an upper bound on behavioural mispricing because of risk-neutral vs physical measure.

raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Risk-neutral is not physical probability (risk premium can justify part of the gap); basis between oracle/settlement source and option underlying; shorting YES = buying NO ties up (1-p) capital; finance-category taker fee 0.04; thin depth on threshold strikes.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Daily snapshot of all live commodity/crypto threshold markets vs Breeden-Litzenberger digitals for 30 days; trade only gaps > 2x estimated cost in paper mode; check that convergence, not resolution luck, drives PnL.
raw_discovery_candidates.adjacent_grounding: Classic digital-option replication and the sportsbook-vs-exchange convergence literature; same logic as the 'do prediction markets match option prices' tests run on election/Fed contracts.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Options-implied versus Polymarket crypto threshold stat-arb
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Trade the gap between Polymarket 'BTC above X by date' prices and the digital value implied by listed options, delta-hedged.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: For each threshold market compute the risk-neutral binary value from a listed call spread on the same strike and maturity (Binance or Deribit). Polymarket Yes prices sit persistently above the option-implied value, most at low probabilities and long maturities, and the gap mean-reverts with a half-life of about four hours. The agent sells the rich side on Polymarket (or buys No), hedges delta on the options/perp venue and unwinds as the gap closes.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Segmented venues; speculative demand for cheap Yes on Polymarket; slow information transmission.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: The wedge is statistically strong, but the tradable proxy was only marginally significant after costs, and the main sample is 2023, before fees and before professional makers arrived.

evidence.title: Do Prediction Markets Match Option Prices? Bitcoin Threshold Evidence from Binance and Polymarket (Portnaya)
evidence.supports: Mean gap 5.6 pp over 214 hourly observations (t=6.46), 6.3 pp pooled over 287; AR(1) half-life ~4 h; 11 pp versus Deribit; delta-hedged proxy profitable after conservative costs 'with marginal statistical precision'. Main sample September 2023 [pre-2025 data, possibly stale].

raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Stale sample; crypto taker fee 0.07 now applies; resolution source differences (Chainlink TWAP vs option settlement index); borrow/margin on the hedge leg.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Recompute the gap for current weekly/monthly BTC threshold markets against Deribit for two weeks; check that the 2023 sign and size still hold.
raw_discovery_candidates.adjacent_grounding: Same paper (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19517) is the grounding; it is itself the adjacent-field test (options literature applied to Polymarket).

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Options-implied relative value: fade overpriced crypto threshold and touch binaries against the Deribit or IBIT surface
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Polymarket 'BTC above or hits X' prices sit about 5-11 pp above option-implied probabilities. Sell the binary, preferably as a maker, and hedge the tail with a call spread if you want.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Fit a volatility surface (SVI or SSVI) to Deribit or IBIT options. Terminal 'above K' markets price as N(d2) or a tight call spread divided by its width. 'Hits K by T' markets price as one-touch, roughly twice the delta, or by the reflection principle. Compare these with Polymarket. The documented wedge is positive, persistent with a half-life of about 4 hours, and largest at low implied probabilities and long maturities. Sell YES, or buy NO, where the wedge exceeds fees, and hedge with a vertical spread. Mismatches matter: the Binance BTCUSDT reference against IBIT or the Deribit index, and the expiry date against the resolution date.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Retail longshot and volatility demand on Polymarket, against a professional options market they cannot easily arbitrage. Access and fungibility are limited, and both legs must be fully collateralised.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: Professionals find the margin treatment unattractive because the short binary is 100% collateralised with no offset against Deribit. A small team that accepts the capital inefficiency can harvest what amounts to a variance and longshot premium.
raw_discovery_candidates.adjacent_grounding: Digital and one-touch replication with verticals, and harvesting the variance risk premium.

evidence.title: Do Prediction Markets Match Option Prices? Bitcoin Threshold Evidence from Binance and Polymarket
evidence.supports: Polymarket YES was on average 5.6 pp above the Binance-option-implied value (t=6.46). The pooled gap was 6.3 pp and 11 pp against Deribit. The wedge is largest at low probabilities and long maturities, with an AR(1) half-life of about 4 h. Delta-hedged net alpha was 0.067 (t=2.10) on only 16 trades. The sample is from 2023 [pre-2025 data, possibly stale].

evidence.title: Polymarket Overprices Volatility (Mike Platt)
evidence.supports: Worked trade: buy an IBIT Mar 62/63 call spread and sell 95 Polymarket '$110k by Mar 31' contracts. It returns 32-131% if there is no touch. It lists the basis risks: expiry a week early, the Binance reference, and IBIT tracking.

evidence.title: Prediction Market Arbitrage: Using Option Chains to Find Mispriced Bets (Kris Abdelmessih)
evidence.supports: An ex-options market maker's recipe: vertical price divided by width approximates P(above), and one-touch approximates twice the delta. His example has a BTC $250k contract at 9% on Kalshi against about 3.6% from a lognormal model.

evidence.title: beshsigma/polymarket-deribit-pricing
evidence.supports: Reality check: Polymarket touch markets systematically overprice against realised touch frequency, but the apparent 5-130x mispricing 'largely evaporates'. It is the variance risk premium plus favorite-longshot bias. The edge is thin with real tail risk.

evidence.title: Probability Arbitrage: How to Beat Polymarket Using Deribit Options
evidence.supports: Claims '$150k+ profit' from N(d2) against up/down markets. The author is selling the bot and nothing is verified. Treat as a lead.

evidence.title: djienne SSVI plus Breeden-Litzenberger probability engine with backtester
evidence.supports: A reference implementation with edge thresholds of 2.4% and 1.8%. No results are published.

raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: The short-tail payoff is one touch against many wins. Capital is locked for months at 100% collateral. There is reference-index and expiry basis risk. The crypto taker fee of 0.07 applies if you cross. The wedge is a risk premium, not a free lunch.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: A daily snapshot job for 30 days that records the Polymarket ladder against the Deribit-implied ladder. Record the wedge by moneyness and tenor, then the realised outcomes.
raw_discovery_candidates.flags: Deribit and Polymarket access depends on jurisdiction.
